This is first appeal under Section 14(A)(2) of the Scheduled Castes & Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (as amended by the Act of 2015), filed by the appellant against the order dated 26.07.2023 passed by the Special Judge, Ujjain, whereby the application filed by the appellant under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. has been dismissed in connection with FIR/Crime No.281/2022 registered at Police Station Unhel, District Ujjain for commission of offences punishable under Sections 366, 342, 376(2)(n) and 506 of IPC alongwith 3(1)(w)(ii) and 3(2)(v) of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.

sentences.text: 2. Prosecution story in brief is that the prosecutrix belongs to Scheduled Castes community.
Before the incident, in the month of June, 2022, the appellant had come to the house of prosecutrix for construction work of toilet in her house.
Co-accused Radhabai was alongwith the appellant.
Radhabai had introduced the appellant as a Hindu to the prosecutrix.
The prosecutrix and the appellant used to have telephonic conversations.
On 19.07.2022, the appellant by messaging the prosecutrix, had called her outside her home and then he told her that he likes her and asked her to come alongwith him.
When the prosecutrix denied, then the appellant intimidated her that he will kill her mother and brother.
On this, the prosecutrix went with the appellant.
On the false pretext of marriage, appellant took her in a jungle and committed rape upon her.
Thereafter, appellant took the prosecutrix to many places by means of public transport and kept her in a rented room in Jaora.
There too, the appellant committed rape upon the prosecutrix.
After that, appellant took the prosecutrix to a Mosque and forcibly made the prosecutrix wear Burkha, then the prosecutrix doubted that the appellant is not a Hindu but Muslim.
Thereafter, appellant took the prosecutrix to a Mosque in Ahmedabad and kept there in a room for 02 days and committed rape upon her.
Maternal aunt of the appellant came there and called the appellant with name of "Mobin".
In this way, the appellant impersonated himself as Hindu and gave false promise to marry her and committed rape upon her several times.
On 26.07.2022, statement u/S 164 of Cr.P.C. of the prosecutrix was recorded by the concerned Magistrate.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant/accused submits that the appellant has not committed the offence and he has falsely been implicated in the case.
The prosecutrix lived with the appellant for 05 days voluntarily and she was a consenting party for the sexual intercourse.
At the time of incident, the prosecutrix was a major lady.
No internal or external injuries were found on the body of the prosecutrix.

Further, it was submitted that the prosecutrix (PW/1) and her mother (PW/2)
have been examined before the Trial Court.
As per statement of prosecutrix, it is clear that the prosecutrix was a consenting party.
Appellant is in custody since 24.07.2022.
Trial will take considerable long time for its disposal, therefore, it is prayed that the appellant be released on bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/State has opposed the prayer and submits that one criminal case of likewise this offence is also pending against the appellant.
He is a habitual offender therefore, the appellant is not entitled for bail.

5. Having considered the rival submissions and after perusal of the case-diary so also considering the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the view that it is not a fit case to grant bail to the appellant.
Resultantly, present appeal is dismissed.

(PRAKASH CHANDRA GUPTA) JUDGE gp Mobin vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84825133/
